AgXeed’s VCU brings existing tractors into the autonomous fold

 29-06 | Autonomous/semi-autosteering systems | News

LinkedInFacebookXWhatsAppPrint

The unit connects via ISOBUS TIM to link the tractor’s controls to TraXwise, AgXeed’s own planning and monitoring platform. Photos: AgXeed

AgXeed has introduced its Vehicle Control Unit (VCU), a compact retrofit kit that brings existing tractors into the company’s automated ecosystem. The unit connects via ISOBUS TIM to link the tractor’s controls to TraXwise, AgXeed’s own planning and monitoring platform – allowing standard machines to carry out pre-planned operations with little manual input. The VCU has now been added to the Future Farming Autonomous Retrofit Kits Catalogue.

According to Arjan Mulder, Chief Commercial Officer at AgXeed, the benefits of the system lie precisely in that software layer. ‘AgXeed’s technological strength lies in TraXwise, the company’s own planning and monitoring platform supplied with the VCU’, he explains.

Through TraXwise, a farmer or manager can plan the entire working route in advance – down to the level of individual fields with varying bed dimensions. ‘Our customer guidance pattern allows you to pre-plan everything, even when you have varying dimensions – say five beds of one metre ten, then a three-metre tramline, then five beds again’, Mulder says.

‘It might sound like a small detail, but for vegetable growers it has real practical value. By shifting ten centimetres on one side, growers can fit an entire bed in a single pass – and that can all be planned in advance, in winter already, as soon as the field has been measured. The alternative – taking the tractor into the field and measuring everything manually – takes more time and is more prone to error.’

 The VCU is aimed at arable farms, vegetable growers and large-scale farming operations.Multi-brand by design

Once mounted, the VCU links the tractor’s controls to TraXwise, allowing standard vehicles to carry out pre-planned operations – including turns and implement use – in a highly automated way. AgXeed positions the VCU’s most distinctive feature as the ability to pre-plan every operation, both route and implements, from a single place. The system is designed to work as one connected, multi-brand platform that ensures consistent execution, reducing operator stress while enabling live monitoring of the whole farm from one interface.

Navigation is handled via GPS with RTK correction, with the vehicle following pre-planned guidance lines generated in TraXwise. The VCU supports autonomous forward and reverse manoeuvring, although with trailed implements, reverse manoeuvres still need to be carried out manually. The system can also perform autonomous headland turns in tight spaces, matched to the tractor’s calibrated turning radius; tighter situations can still be handled manually where needed. Autonomous working speed ranges from 0 to 20 km/h.

Implement control over ISOBUS TIM

Implements are controlled over ISOBUS TIM, with the tractor functioning as the TIM server and the VCU as the client. A TCU for implement monitoring can also be connected to the ISOBUS plug, and standard ISOBUS features on implements remain available throughout. If an implement requires a TIM functionality not supported by the VCU, that function is simply left unused.

At its current stage, the VCU functions as a highly automated system in which the driver supervises the surrounding environment. Errors are displayed on the in-cab tablet, and the tractor stops automatically in the event of a connection loss. An RTK fallback function maintains positioning for eight to 10 minutes if satellite signal is lost. Remote supervision is possible via TraXwise, though one operator cannot yet supervise multiple machines simultaneously – tasks can, however, be planned and dispatched to several machines at once.

The VCU is aimed at arable farms, vegetable growers and large-scale farming operations. AgXeed says further integration is in development for when the ISOBUS TIM standard is ready for higher levels of autonomy, including Level 4 autonomy, as well as integration of vehicle data not currently transferred over the TIM protocol.

 The VCU can be moved to another compatible tractor simply by unplugging the cables and removing the unit from its roof-mounted bracket.Easy to transfer between tractors

AgXeed’s main commercially active countries are Germany, the Netherlands, Australia, Ukraine and Austria, with additional unit support in Canada and the USA. Commercial status is currently limited release for 2026, with full commercial rollout planned for 2027.

One practical advantage highlighted by AgXeed is transferability: the VCU can be moved to another compatible tractor simply by unplugging the cables and removing the unit from its roof-mounted bracket. Initial installation requires more time, since the navigation antenna must be positioned and the system calibrated for turning radii and antenna placement, and cabling must be routed to the in-cab connector. Once installed, however, the VCU can be quickly removed and relocated – either to another vehicle or for secure storage.

The VCU is priced at €12.500 (US $14,238 at the exchange rate of 29 June 2026), including one year of subscriptions covering RTK, data and TraXwise. Annual software and service costs thereafter amount to €1.300 (US $1,481).

translationZh:
AgXeed推出了其车辆控制单元（VCU），这是一款紧凑型改装套件，可将现有拖拉机纳入该公司的自动化生态系统。该单元通过ISOBUS TIM连接，将拖拉机的控制与AgXeed自有的规划与监控平台TraXwise相连——使标准机械能够在少量人工干预下执行预先规划的操作。VCU现已加入《未来农业自主改装套件目录》。

据AgXeed首席商务官Arjan Mulder介绍，该系统的优势恰恰在于其软件层。他解释道：“AgXeed的技术优势在于TraXwise，这是随VCU提供的公司自有规划与监控平台。”

通过TraXwise，农民或管理者可以提前规划整个作业路线——精确到具有不同畦宽的单个地块。“我们的客户引导模式允许您预先规划一切，即使地块尺寸各异——比如五条一米一宽的畦，然后是一条三米宽的作业道，接着又是五条畦，”Mulder说。

“这听起来像是一个小细节，但对蔬菜种植者来说具有实际价值。通过在一侧偏移十厘米，种植者可以在一次通过中完成整畦作业——这都可以提前规划，甚至在冬季田地测量完成后即可进行。而另一种方式——将拖拉机开进地里手动测量——耗时更多且更容易出错。”

VCU面向大田农场、蔬菜种植者以及大规模农业作业。

**多品牌设计**

安装后，VCU将拖拉机的控制与TraXwise连接，使标准车辆能够以高度自动化的方式执行预先规划的操作——包括转弯和农具使用。AgXeed将VCU最显著的特点定位为能够从单一平台预先规划每项操作，包括路线和农具。该系统设计为一个互联的多品牌平台，确保一致的执行，减轻操作员压力，同时通过单一界面实时监控整个农场。

导航通过带RTK校正的GPS处理，车辆遵循TraXwise中生成的预规划引导线。VCU支持自主前进和倒退操作，但使用牵引式农具时，倒退操作仍需手动完成。系统还能在狭窄空间内执行自主地头转弯，与拖拉机标定的转弯半径匹配；更复杂的情况仍可手动处理。自主作业速度范围为0至20公里/小时。

**通过ISOBUS TIM控制农具**

农具通过ISOBUS TIM控制，拖拉机作为TIM服务器，VCU作为客户端。用于农具监控的TCU也可连接到ISOBUS插头，农具上的标准ISOBUS功能在整个过程中保持可用。如果农具需要VCU不支持的TIM功能，该功能将被忽略。

目前，VCU作为高度自动化系统运行，驾驶员负责监控周围环境。错误显示在驾驶室内的平板电脑上，连接中断时拖拉机会自动停止。如果卫星信号丢失，RTK后备功能可维持定位8至10分钟。通过TraXwise可实现远程监控，但目前一名操作员尚不能同时监控多台机器——不过，任务可以同时规划和分派给多台机器。

VCU面向大田农场、蔬菜种植者以及大规模农业作业。AgXeed表示，正在开发进一步集成，以适应ISOBUS TIM标准未来支持更高水平自主性（包括4级自主）的需求，以及集成当前未通过TIM协议传输的车辆数据。

**易于在拖拉机之间转移**

AgXeed的主要商业活跃国家包括德国、荷兰、澳大利亚、乌克兰和奥地利，并在加拿大和美国提供额外支持。目前商业状态为2026年限量发布，2027年全面商业推广。

AgXeed强调的一个实际优势是可转移性：只需拔掉电缆并从车顶支架上取下单元，即可将VCU移至另一台兼容拖拉机。初始安装需要更多时间，因为必须定位导航天线、标定转弯半径和天线位置，并将电缆布线至驾驶室连接器。但一旦安装完成，VCU可以快速拆卸和重新定位——无论是转移到另一台车辆还是安全存放。

VCU定价为12,500欧元（按2026年6月29日汇率约合14,238美元），包含一年的RTK、数据和TraXwise订阅。此后每年的软件和服务费用为1,300欧元（约合1,481美元）。
